question.problem:
Find the value of the constant $a$ that makes the function $g(x)$ below continuous at $x=2.$

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{3}^{2ax+1}, & x\le 2 \\ 2x+5, & x>2\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=2,$ the left-sided limit is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}g(x) & =g(2) \\  & ={3}^{2a(2)+1} \\  & ={3}^{4a+1},\end{aligned}
$$

 

At $x=2,$ the right-sided limit is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}(2x+5) \\  & =2(2)+5 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=2,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{4a+1} & =9 \\ {3}^{4a+1} & ={3}^{2} \\ 4a+1 & =2 \\ 4a & =1 \\ a & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $g(x)$ is continuous at $x=2$ for $a=\frac{1}{4}.$
